text:
Aisha: quick ask - prospect Nimbus wants a private/vpc poc next week. hard reqs: SAML assertions must never traverse the public internet, they prefer ipv6 for client traffic, and they want a short non-technical justification PrivateLink vs Peering for security reviewers. can netops + security advise? cc @Tom :wave:

Tom: TL;DR: PrivateLink = endpoint-level isolation + much narrower firewall allowlist and no cross-account route injection. VPC Peering = cheaper (no connector surcharge) but gives broader L3 reachability and requires careful route table scoping. if SAML absolutely cannot leave their network, recommend either private deployment or run a tiny SAML-proxy in their VPC that forwards over PrivateLink.

Diego: IPv6 callout: our hosted PrivateLink connector speaks IPv4 only today. we can support ipv6 client traffic via customer-side NAT64/translation gateway, but native v6 for hosted PrivateLink is not GA. flag as a blocker if they insist on native ipv6 for the connector. control-plane (saml) can be proxied over ipv4 PrivateLink.

Tom: minimal firewall allowlist (example CIDRs):
```
# outbound from customer app/subnets -> Redwood endpoints
TCP 443 -> 35.199.100.0/22   # control-plane callbacks / auth
TCP 443 -> 52.210.16.0/22    # model-serving endpoints (hosted)
# optional: ICMP echo to 35.199.100.0/22 for health checks
# if they require static egress IPs for callbacks: allow TCP 443 from our EIP pool (we will share exact list)
```

sec-bot: FYI - prospect checked "no shared IPs". PrivateLink provides per-endpoint isolation but does not guarantee single-tenant hardware. if they require physical/dedicated hosts, open a dedicated-hosting request/ticket. :lock:

Aisha: thanks. can we meet 2pm PT today to finalize the one-page justification + pre-provision checklist to hand to the customer? i'll include recommendations for SAML-bridge steps if needed.

Tom: 2pm works for me - i'll bring the exact connector CIDRs and a short routing snippet.

Diego: in. i'll bring the nat64 notes and the list of limitations for dual-stack.

Aisha: great, i'll schedule and send the draft after the call. :thumbsup:
